qualitative.filing_summary_10k: For fiscal 2026, Everpure (formerly Pure Storage) reported total revenue of $3.66 billion, up 16% year-over-year, split between product revenue ($1.97 billion, up 16%) and subscription services revenue ($1.69 billion, up 15%). Subscription ARR grew 16% to $1.92 billion with Net Dollar Retention of 113%, and total Remaining Performance Obligations reached $3.7 billion, up 40%. The company held $1.5 billion in cash and marketable securities, established a new $500 million revolving credit facility, repurchased $342.5 million of stock, and entered a definitive agreement in February 2026 to acquire 1touch, a data intelligence and governance company.
qualitative.filing_summary_10q: This 10-Q covers the quarter ended August 2, 2026, filed by Everpure, Inc. (formerly Pure Storage) under ticker P. The provided excerpt is largely XBRL tagging data and cover-page information rather than narrative disclosure, but it confirms the company completed its previously announced acquisition of 1touch on May 7, 2026, and had 333,227,251 Class A shares outstanding as of August 31, 2026. Detailed financial results and MD&A narrative for the quarter were not included in the excerpt provided.
qualitative.filing_summary_8k: This 8-K, dated August 26, 2026, discloses under Item 2.02 that Everpure issued a press release and planned a conference call regarding its financial results for the quarter ended August 2, 2026, with the press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The filing notes that non-GAAP financial measures are referenced in the press release and reconciled to GAAP figures within it, and this information is furnished rather than filed for Exchange Act purposes.
qualitative.moat_explanation: The 10-K describes a subscription-based Evergreen architecture that locks customers into continuous, non-disruptive hardware/software refreshes rather than discrete purchases, and reports Subscription Net Dollar Retention of 113%-117% and $3.7 billion of largely non-cancelable Remaining Performance Obligations, both of which suggest customers renew and expand rather than switch providers. The company also frames its platform as unifying data management across on-premises, cloud and edge environments, which would raise the operational cost/risk of migrating away once adopted, though the excerpts don't quantify actual switching costs or competitor comparisons directly.
red_flags: Company expects product gross margin to sequentially decline in the next quarter due to higher component costs.
A single hyperscaler customer is called out repeatedly as a major growth driver (design win, incremental investment to scale supply chain for it), suggesting meaningful customer concentration risk.
Full valuation allowance maintained against U.S. deferred tax assets, including NOL carryforwards, indicating a history of not consistently generating U.S. taxable income.
Prior-year restructuring and impairment charges (workforce reduction and lease abandonment) reflect earlier cost-cutting and facility downsizing.

Reliance on third-party contract manufacturers and supply chain partners for hardware production and hyperscaler shipments, with company noting inventory build-up to mitigate tariffs and supply disruptions.
